title: POC privacy workshop & retention playbook
body:
Context:
This is a working playbook from the Aug 2025 SE workshop focused on recommended retention/handling patterns and a lightweight DPA addendum skeleton that we can include in POC proposals. Primary goal: provide repeatable, low-friction options for customers doing supervised POCs or evals with sensitive inputs (PII, PHI, customer IP). Not legal advice — draft language for internal review and customer negotiation.

Attendees (workshop):
- Maya Patel (owner) - SE lead
- Liam Chen - applied ML
- Sofia Martinez - product security
- Arjun Rao - infra/dedicated
- Emily Carter - customer success
- Jordan Blake - legal (observing)

High-level POC constraints we see repeatedly:
- Short evaluation windows (1–6 weeks) with heavy sampling of user queries.
- Customers want fast time-to-result; minimal ops/config changes.
- Varying risk tolerance: startups vs regulated enterprise.
- Desire to avoid sending persistent training-style datasets to hosted APIs.

Suggested retention profiles (pick one in proposal):
1) Ephemeral-mode (default, lowest friction)
   - Behavior: all inference logs and transcript data are deleted automatically after 24 hours.
   - Storage: no user-provided data persisted beyond 24h; caching disabled for the POC.
   - Notes: ideal for public cloud hosted API POCs where customer cannot provide network restrictions.

2) Short-term hashed logs (compromise)
   - Behavior: raw inputs retained for up to 7 days for debugging, then purged.
   - Hashing: store SHA-256 of input payloads for dedup/analytics; raw content only in encrypted store accessible to SEs for debugging.
   - Access: access to raw data limited to named SEs and CS for a defined troubleshooting window.

3) Customer-managed retention (enterprise)
   - Behavior: customer supplies S3/GCS endpoint or VPC peering to push logs; Redwood does not keep persistent copies by default.
   - Option: provide tokenized or masked returns; KMS integration for customer keys.
   - Notes: requires longer lead time and security signoffs.

4) Air-gapped / on-prem POC (highest isolation)
   - Behavior: Redwood Private deployed; no egress; all artifacts remain on customer infra; Redwood support via SSH bastion and audited sessions.

Runtime protections (applies across profiles):
- Disable mem-caching for POC sessions unless explicitly agreed.
- Prompt redaction hooks: configurable pipeline stage to strip SSNs, credit cards using regex before they reach model. Not a replacement for customer pre-processing.
- Tokenization audit: store only token counts for business metrics when in ephemeral mode.

DPA addendum draft (skeleton clauses for inclusion in POC SOW) — language to hand to legal:
- Purpose-limited processing: Customer Data will be used solely for the evaluation of the POC and related troubleshooting; no model training or product improvement uses are permitted without Customer’s prior written consent.
- Retention and deletion: Redwood will retain Customer Data only for the period expressly agreed in the SOW (e.g., 24 hours, 7 days, or customer-managed). After the retention period Redwood will irreversibly delete Customer Data from active systems and backups as soon as reasonably possible.
- Access controls: Access to Customer Data is restricted to authorized personnel with a documented business need; all access is logged and subject to periodic review.
- Encryption and keys: Customer Data in transit and at rest will be encrypted using TLS and AES-256; for customer-managed retention the customer may supply and manage KMS keys.
- Subprocessors: Any subprocessors used for the POC will be listed in the SOW and bound by similar obligations.
- Incident response: Redwood will notify Customer within 72 hours of becoming aware of any confirmed data breach affecting Customer Data and will cooperate in investigation and remediation.
- Audit & compliance: For enterprise POCs Redwood will permit one onsite or remote audit during the POC, with 30 days’ notice.

Practical wording variants (short form) to add in non-legal SOWs:
- "POC data retention mode: EPHEMERAL (24h) — Redwood will remove content after 24 hours and will not use content for model training or product analytics unless otherwise agreed."
- "Logs mode: LIMITED (7d) — Redwood will retain raw logs for up to 7 days for troubleshooting; thereafter logs will be deleted. Access limited to named SEs and CS staff."
- "Customer-managed — No persistent copies kept by Redwood unless explicitly agreed; customer provides storage/KMS."

Data flow (textual map) — include this in proposal diagrams:
- Client app -> Redwood API (HTTPS) -> Inference runtime (optionally: prefix KV cache) -> Response -> Optional transient log stream -> Retention store (per profile)
- Debug path: infra-only encrypted bucket (7d) -> SE access via access request ticket (audit trail)

Open questions & risk flags (to resolve pre-sale):
- Backups: how to guarantee purge from long-lived backups within SLA window? Need infra confirmation from SRE on snapshot lifecycle. (Action: Arjun to confirm by 2025-08-18).
- Legal sign-off threshold: what retention options require legal involvement? Standardize threshold (e.g., >7 days or any PHI). (Action: Maya + Jordan).
- Monitoring vs retention: analytics we collect (token counts, latency) — ensure aggregate metrics are allowed under the POC retention profile. (Action: Liam).
- Redaction accuracy: regex-based redaction can miss edge cases — recommend customer-side pre-processing for regulated data.

Example POC proposals (snippets) to reuse in SOWs:
- Short POC (2 weeks, default): EPHEMERAL 24h retention, no caching, Redwood will provide debugging access for 48h after reported incidents.
- Extended evaluation (up to 6 weeks): LIMITED 7d retention, named SE access, weekly status call, customer-managed KMS available.
- Enterprise guarded POC: private deployment / VPC; Redwood support via secure bastion; retention per customer policy; audit rights included.

Workshop action items (owners & dates):
- Arjun Rao: confirm backup snapshot Purge RT policy and mapping to retention profiles — due 2025-08-18.
- Jordan Blake: produce a 1-page legal concierge note describing when legal must be engaged (PHI, >7d retention, enterprise on-prem) — due 2025-08-22.
- Liam Chen: add instrumentation plan to capture only aggregate telemetry for ephemeral mode; update observability docs — due 2025-08-25.
- Maya Patel: compile two SOW templates (24h and 7d) using the phrasing above and circulate — due 2025-08-19.
- Sofia Martinez: draft a customer checklist for pre-POC security questionnaire (network, keys, compliance requirements) — due 2025-08-21.

Quick troubleshooting playbook for SEs (cheat-sheet):
- Customer reports unexpected retention -> confirm POC profile, check ingestion logs, raise access ticket if raw payloads are present in debug bucket.
- If raw payloads exist outside agreed window -> escalate to Arjun + legal and freeze access.
- For debugging: request time-limited access (24h) and capture audit IDs.

Notes to self (informal):
- Need a simple checkbox in the POC creation flow that sets one of the profiles and attaches the DPA clause automatically. Product should make the default be EPHEMERAL.
- Consider adding a one-click opt-in for customers to allow short-term troubleshooting access that is logged and requires explicit approver.

Appendix: sample short DPA clause (copy/paste friendly)
"Customer Data. For the purposes of this SOW, 'Customer Data' means any input, prompt, file, or other content provided by Customer to Redwood in connection with the POC. Redwood will process Customer Data solely to perform the POC and related troubleshooting. Unless otherwise agreed in writing, Redwood will not use Customer Data to improve models or services. Redwood will retain Customer Data only for the retention period selected in the SOW (e.g., 24 hours), after which Redwood will delete such data from active systems and reasonable backups as soon as practicable."

End notes / references:
- See CONFLUENCE-1234 (POC security baseline) for more detailed checklist.
- Related ticket: JIRA-SERV-887 (POC creation flow feature request).
- Keep this doc terse; hand off to legal for final DPA drafting.

Last updated by Maya Patel on 2025-08-20.
